Can anyone please explain this question.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Here you can only do (b) given the permissions of the file.

  • FileA.txt does not have r for u, so User1 cannot read that file using cat.
  • FileB.txt does not have w set for u (or anyone), so User1 cannot write to that file using >>.
  • FileD.txt has r set for u, so User1 can read it using cat.
  • More_Files does not have r set for u (or anyone), so User1 cannot list its contents using ls.

posts.name: Ayush Das
posts.cooked:
For FileA.txt, if r permission was there for admin only and not for group and others, would it still work ?
For More_Files, r permission only required for admin , same for FileB, w permission only required for admin?

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: Can you clarify what do you mean by admin?

posts.name: Ayush Das
posts.cooked: the first permissions are admin permissions, second group permissions, third others permissions, is my understanding wrong?

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: There is no terminology of admin here, first set is for the owner user, second for the owner group, third for everyone else. Yes if you are the owner and owner permissions does not allow some action, you cannot perform that.
